headline: Revenue growth accelerates, margins widen across regions
summary_short: Equinix's Q2 2026 revenue rose to $2.625B, up 16.4% y/y and 7.4% q/q, while diluted EPS climbed to $4.83 (+28.8% y/y) as operating income grew 34.6% y/y to $665M.
summary_long: Revenue grew across all three regions: Americas +25% (24% cc) on incremental joint-venture services, IBX expansion, and stronger customer demand; EMEA +10% and Asia-Pacific +9%, both on new capacity and order growth. Cost of revenue rose largely on IBX-expansion depreciation and higher utility costs, but revenue growth outpaced expenses, lifting operating income 34.6% y/y. Annualized gross bookings reached $424M, up 23% y/y. FFO rose to $854M (+24% y/y) and AFFO to $1.17B (+20% y/y). Cash and short-term investments fell as the company funded $1.58B of capex and paid a $5.16/share dividend, up from $4.69 a year ago; long-term debt rose modestly to $19.9B. No numeric forward guidance was found in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based growth: Americas +25% (24% cc) on incremental joint-venture services and IBX expansion; EMEA +10% and Asia-Pacific +9%, both on new IBX capacity and stronger orders from existing and new customers.

Margin widened because revenue grew faster than cost of revenue (16.4% vs 13.5% y/y), as a majority of cost of revenue (depreciation, rent, utilities) is largely fixed against a growing recurring-revenue base.
Grew faster than revenue as cost of revenue (+13.5% y/y) and other operating expenses rose more slowly than the 16.4% y/y revenue increase.

Tracks operating income's growth from the same revenue-outpacing-costs dynamic; the modest gap to operating income reflects differing treatment of non-operating items between Yahoo's EBIT figure and the SEC operating-income line.
Rose 18.1% y/y, slower than EBIT's 24.8%, because the D&A added back also grew as new IBX capacity was placed into service during the past year.

Company states net income increased $110 million (30%) in the quarter, driven by revenue and operating growth described above, partly offset by higher interest expense from 2026/2025 senior note issuances and higher other expense from equity-method investments.
Rose with net income growth, slightly diluted by a modestly higher weighted-average diluted share count (99.1M vs 98.1M a year ago).

Management cited AI-driven hyperscale demand accelerating power consumption per cabinet, a $459M Hampton Campus sale to a joint venture, and Annualized Gross Bookings of $424M (+23% y/y) as the quarter's core themes.
